issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for ExcellenceLand boolean attribute: the UML/problem statement declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' (problem_statement.md line 36), while the solution implementation defines a boolean field named 'isExcellent' and a getter isExcellent() (src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java line 8). This discrepancy between the attribute name in the specification and the field/getter name in the code can confuse students about the exact attribute they must declare, the constructor parameter name, and the expected getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent between the UML/problem statement, template and implementation. Either: (A) Rename the boolean field in the code from 'isExcellent' to 'excellentEnough', accept it as the second constructor parameter named 'excellentEnough', and provide a public getter matching the chosen convention (e.g., isExcellentEnough() or getExcellentEnough()); or (B) update the UML/problem statement to use 'isExcellent' so the specification and code match. Ensure all references (constructor parameter name and getter) are updated accordingly so students have a single, unambiguous attribute name to implement.
